facts.old: Linearizable: every read sees the latest write, as if single-copy; costs coordination; needed for locks, leader state, exactly-one invariants
facts.where: Reading, Linearizability (Jepsen definition, real-time order, history B)
facts.verdict: verified; made precise (real-time ordering)

facts.old: Sequential / causal: causally related ops are ordered everywhere; concurrent ops may interleave differently
facts.where: Reading, correction box under Consistency models; lab history 6
facts.verdict: corrected: the sentence describes causal only; sequential requires one total order seen by all (Jepsen, Sequential)

facts.old: Causal+ is the sweet spot for geo-replicated data
facts.where: Reading, same correction box
facts.verdict: labelled opinion; attributed to the COPS paper (Lloyd et al., SOSP 2011) and Jepsen's note on causal+

facts.old: Eventual: replicas converge given quiet time; fine for feature flags, model registries, usage counters
facts.where: Reading, Eventual consistency (DynamoDB default quote); examples replaced by the chat product's sidebar and chat list
facts.verdict: verified; examples generalised to 'per piece of data' in the One screen habit and PACELC paragraph

facts.old: Serializable is about isolation, orthogonal to linearizability; strict serializability is both
facts.where: Reading, Linearizable is not serializable
facts.verdict: verified (Jepsen, Strong Serializability)

facts.old: Default to the weakest level the invariant tolerates; make the invariant explicit (billing must not double-charge vs dashboard 30s stale)

facts.old: Delivery semantics: at-most-once, at-least-once (default), exactly-once impossible (Two Generals) -> exactly-once processing via dedup (idempotency keys, Kafka transactional producer + idempotent consumer offsets, SQS FIFO dedup IDs); say effectively-once

facts.old: Single-writer systems need one node elected with consensus: Raft (etcd, Consul, Kafka KRaft) or Paxos family (Chubby, Spanner)
facts.where: Reading, Consensus and What real systems choose (etcd, Kafka KRaft 4.0, Spanner Paxos, DynamoDB Multi-Paxos)
facts.verdict: verified (Raft paper; Kafka 4.0 announcement; Spanner paper; Elhemali 2022); Consul named only (not re-read)

facts.old: Never hand-roll; take a lease/lock from etcd or ZooKeeper
facts.where: Reading, consensus cost box and Common mistakes
facts.verdict: kept; evidence added (Jepsen Redis-Raft 21 issues)

facts.old: Keep the lease TTL well above GC pauses
facts.where: Reading, correction box in Leader election, leases and fencing tokens
facts.verdict: corrected: a longer TTL only makes failure rarer; Jepsen etcd 3.4.3 lost ~18% of acknowledged updates with 2 s TTLs and pauses, and mutual exclusion failed in healthy clusters
